title: Priority Lanes & Critical-Skill Shadowing Protocol for Cycle Capacity
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable protocol for assigning 'priority lanes' across initiatives and pairing engineers in short-term 'critical-skill shadowing' shifts to reduce single-owner risk during the cycle. This protocol should enable predictable scope cuts, surface capacity limits early, and ensure critical roles (runtime ops, kernel tuning, Dedicated autoscale) have at least one shadowed backup for the hot weeks of a cycle.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page protocol doc exists in Confluence and is linked from cycle planning playbooks
Priority lane taxonomy (Core SLO, High-Visibility Customer, Infra Risk, Growth Experiments) defined and agreed by PM/Eng/Design
Shadowing roster created for all critical roles covering 80% of high-risk weekdays in the cycle
Three staffed cross-roll lanes for emergency surge that can be activated within 24 hours
A decision rubric for scope trims tied to lane priorities is documented and used in at least one mid-cycle trim exercise
implementation_steps: Draft protocol and taxonomy with engineering leads and product managers
Run one tabletop exercise simulating a critical-role outage and validate shadow handoff within 8 hours
Publish Confluence doc with roster template and rotation calendar
Integrate protocol into cycle kickoff agenda and capacity planning spreadsheet
Create three Linear child tickets to staff and verify initial rosters
rollback_plan: If adoption is low after two weeks, pause mandatory shadowing and switch to voluntary on-call pairing while collecting feedback. Re-evaluate after one cycle and pivot the taxonomy or incentives.
metrics_and_signals: % days with at least one shadow assigned for each critical role >= 80%
Number of hours to restore service in tabletop exercise <= 8h
Number of scope-trim decisions made using the priority lane rubric >= 1 per cycle
Post-cycle incident rate for infra regressions reduced by 15% compared to previous cycle
notes: Protocol intentionally lightweight: target 1-page + roster template to minimize process friction
Design will provide a visual lane taxonomy card for the kickoff slide deck
Compensation/recognition plan for shadow participants to be discussed with People ops if rollout expands

risks: Insufficient volunteer coverage for shadowing leading to single-owner outages
Extra coordination overhead may reduce feature throughput if not tightly scoped
Ambiguous lane definitions could create political friction between initiatives
